key_insight: Nitrogen vacancies locally weaken polar-axis lattice coupling in wurtzite AlN, enabling defect-mediated switching whose spatial distribution and timing govern ferroelectric domain growth.
engineering_relevance: Engineering nitrogen vacancies, whose formation is promoted by scandium doping, offers a route to lower coercive fields for low-voltage ferroelectric memory.
method: Density functional theory to investigate vacancy effects and lattice coupling.
Deep Potential molecular dynamics to model polarization switching and domain growth.
Experimental characterization to connect simulations with observed behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that ideal crystals favor polar-axis growth, while vacancy-mediated switching explains experimentally observed nearly isotropic or transverse growth; no quantitative benchmarks are provided.
watch_item: Reliable device implementation requires control of vacancy distribution, and the abstract does not establish endurance or retention trade-offs.
paper_title: Nitrogen vacancy cluster-mediated ferroelectric domain growth in wurtzite AlN
